key_insight: Coherently controlled quantum probes can learn many-body properties that standard response theory cannot access, because probe readout captures anti-commutator and mixed-order correlators beyond nested-commutator susceptibilities.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new measurement paradigm for spectroscopy, microscopy, and quantum sensing where probe-only readout can reveal fluctuations, entanglement, and non-equilibrium structure with resources tied to correlation complexity rather than system size.
method: Quantum-circuit framework unifying spectroscopy, probe microscopy, and probe-based quantum technologies
Probe dynamics used to extract target-system correlators from final probe measurements only
Entangled-probe protocols developed to access quantities such as von Neumann entropy
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical proof and protocol demonstration, showing that probe-based learning is strictly more expressive than conventional response theory and can access observables not reachable by single-probe or system-only measurements.
watch_item: The approach relies on coherent control and entangled probes, so practical performance may be limited by decoherence, control errors, and the difficulty of implementing sufficiently precise probe-target interactions.
paper_title: Quantum probe advantage in learning many-body systems
